info.name: FWA Sales — Supply Chain Dashboard API (local)
info.description:
The admin/web dashboard half of the platform: Device Partner, IOH and MPX.

Run the folders in order with the Postman Runner and it walks a real unit from an IOH-issued number all the way to a salesman's phone. Folder 09 is the point of the whole thing — it logs in as the AE and proves the mobile app can now see the stock.

Re-runnable: folder 02 mints a fresh batch of MSISDNs each run, because numbers are unique platform-wide.

AUTH: three roles are involved, so tokens are per-role collection variables (dpToken / iohToken / mpxToken) rather than one shared token. Each request picks the right one.

item.name: 00 — Sign in (all three roles)
item.description: Each company signs in separately. Note what /admin/me returns: role plus exactly one organisation binding, which is the entire authorisation context for everything that follows.

request.description: Bound to ADVAN. Sees only its own POs.
Global read by design — IOH is the counterparty to every partner.
Bound to MPX-BKL-01. Sees only its own orders, stock and AEs.
The dashboard builds its sidebar from this response.

item.name: 05 An AE token is rejected here

request.description: Proves the audience split. An AE token carries no `aud` claim, so the admin decoder refuses it before any handler runs. Run folder 09 first if aeToken is empty.

item.name: 01 — Reference data
item.description: Master data the forms are built from. Small fixed sets, returned unpaginated.

request.description: Note `kind`: Saldo Mobo is a BALANCE product and carries no quotaGb. Branch on kind, not on the absence of the quota.
Two rows. displayName is the brand (IM3), outletName the storefront (Gerai IM3) — the mockups used both interchangeably.
listPriceIdr may be null, meaning the model has no confirmed price and cannot be ordered.

exec: const m = b.find(x => x.modelCode === 'ADVAN V1 PRO');

request.description: A DP gets 403 here — it has no business enumerating its competitors.
The role boundary, demonstrated.
A DP ships to them, so it needs their names.

item.name: 02 — MSISDN PO (DP asks, IOH supplies)
item.description: The first use case, and the one that exercises every mechanism: org scoping across two companies, a status machine, bulk import with a dry run, and quantity conservation.

item.name: 01 DP raises a request for 5 numbers

request.description: The PO code is generated server-side as {DP}-{YYYYMMDD}-{SEQ} and is never accepted from the client.

exec: // Fresh batch each run: MSISDNs are unique platform-wide, so a re-run would
// otherwise collide with the numbers the last run issued.
for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { list.push('628' + String(seed * 10 + i).padStart(10, '0').slice(-10)); }

request.description: IOH sees every partner's requests. A DP sees only its own.
Transition DIAJUKAN -> DIPROSES.
Writes nothing. The operator must see the parsed numbers before committing them. Note the 08… numbers come back normalised to 62….

All or nothing, and the count must equal qtyRequested exactly. Supplied numbers become fwa_inventory rows at MSISDN_ISSUED with no IMEI — invisible to the mobile app.

Send an Idempotency-Key header and replay it: the original result comes back and nothing is inserted twice.

item.name: 06 A DP cannot supply its own request — expect 403

request.description: The whole point of two organisations is that one cannot do the other's step.
Backs the download icon. xlsx is not offered — it would mean adding a spreadsheet dependency; CSV opens in Excel.

item.name: 03 — Hard-bundle pairing (DP)
item.description: One IMEI per MSISDN. The counts must match exactly — a partial pairing is rejected rather than applied, because half a bundle is a unit nobody can ship and nobody can find.

request.description: The unpaired numbers on this PO.
Shares its checks with the real endpoint, so the preview cannot drift.

exec: const pairs = list.map((m, i) => ({ msisdn: m, imei: String(35000000000000 + seed * 10 + i) }));

request.description: Units move to PAIRED. Every IMEI must be unique platform-wide.

item.name: 04 — Delivery addresses (MPX)
item.description: Required before an MPX can order: the PO carries the address the goods ship to.

request.description: mpxId is absent from the body on purpose — the address belongs to whichever MPX is calling, taken from the token.
Default first, then alphabetical — the PO form preselects the default.

item.name: 05 — Device PO (MPX orders, DP fulfils)
item.description: The mirror image of folder 02: the MPX raises it, the DP acts on it.

request.description: unitPriceIdr is snapshotted from the catalogue here and never read back, so a later price change cannot rewrite a closed order. totalIdr = unitPriceIdr × qty is enforced by a database CHECK.
Transition DIAJUKAN -> DIPROSES.
Each unit must be paired, unattached, and have reached this DP through its own MSISDN PO — that last condition stops a partner attaching a competitor's stock.
Units move to ASSIGNED and pick up the destination MPX. Rows are locked FOR UPDATE so two admins cannot commit the same bundle twice.
statusHistory is what the Riwayat panel renders, straight through. It is trustworthy only because every transition writes a row in the same transaction as the status change.

item.name: 06 — Shipment (DP)
item.description: The screen the UI review found missing entirely: the Riwayat panel already showed a courier and resi, and nothing produced them.

request.description:
courierName is free text — couriers are manual for v1. Writes '{courier} | {awb}' into the status history.

Refused unless every unit is attached: receipt is all-or-nothing, so shipping short guarantees an order that can never be confirmed.
Entered by hand — no courier integration in v1. Each milestone is recorded once; repeating one would draw a bar that goes backwards.
Backs the four-step tracker. Milestones come back in tracker order, so the client renders them without sorting.

item.name: 07 — Goods receipt (MPX)
item.description: One final, all-or-nothing confirmation. If the box is short, the reshipping happens outside this system and the MPX confirms only once the full list has arrived.

request.description: Transition DIKIRIM -> PERIKSA.

Units move to RECEIVED and are stamped with receivedAt — the key automatic allocation orders by.

If units were missing this returns 422 RECEIPT_INCOMPLETE, nothing is written, and the order stays at PERIKSA.

item.name: 08 — Stock & allocation (MPX)
item.description: Where the seam closes. The allocation endpoint is the only writer of fwa_inventory.allocated_ae_id.

request.description: Tersedia = received and unallocated; Dialokasikan = allocated and not yet activated; Total = the two added. A sold unit leaves all three.
Backs the Manual picker. Ordered by receivedAt exactly as automatic allocation would take them.
The endpoint that could not exist on the AE audience: golden rule 2 scopes every AE-facing list to the token, so no AE route returns more than one AE.
The Tentang AE panel: ID, Brand, Branch, and what they hold. brandScope HYBRID means the AE may sell either brand — displayed, not enforced.

THE SEAM. After this the units are visible to that salesman's barcode scanner.

AUTO takes the oldest received units under FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so two admins allocating the last unit produce one success and one clean 409 — never two handovers of the same device.

item.name: 06 Allocating the same units again — expect failure

request.description: A unit is allocated once. Enforced by a unique constraint as well as the row lock.
Tersedia has dropped to 0 and Dialokasikan risen by 5. Total is unchanged: the MPX still holds them, they are just spoken for.

item.name: 09 — Verify on the AE mobile app
item.description: The point of the whole programme. These are the SAME endpoints the Flutter app calls, completely unchanged by this work — the units simply appear now that they have been allocated.

request.description: The mobile app's own login. Untouched by the supply chain work.
Should now include the 5 units just allocated. Before allocation this returned nothing for them — received is not the same as allocated.
The barcode scanner path. Returns eligible: true with the IMEI and modem type resolved server-side — the client never asserts them.
What the app caches for offline use. Carries the same units.

item.name: 05 A supply-chain number is invisible — expect 404

request.description: A number that is not allocated to this AE does not exist as far as the app is concerned. This is the guard that keeps unpaired stock off the scanner.
